data.name: Eyub
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Eyub is the name of Ibrahim's (Abraham) son born to Hagar in the Arabian desert. The name is derived from the Arabic word 'A'yūb, meaning 'living one', due to Hagar's belief that her son would live despite her hardships.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Eyub carries a deep spiritual meaning. It reminds us of the trials and tribulations that we may face in life, and the importance of remaining patient and steadfast in our faith. It also serves as a reminder of the ultimate reward that awaits those who endure suffering with patience and faith.
data.numerology_meaning: Represents spirituality, wisdom, and destiny-driven strength.

in_arabic.name: أيوب
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من ايوب عليه السلام، يعني الصبر والثبات
in_arabic.long_meaning: أيوب هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من اسم النبي أيوب عليه السلام، ويعني الصبر والثبات على الحق، كما ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الأنبياء، الآية 83-84، حيث ذكرت قصة نبي الله أيوب عليه السلام وبلائه وصبره على المرض والابتلاء، مما يجعل الاسم ذا أهمية دينية وروحية كبيرة في الإسلام.

in_urdu.name: ایوب
in_urdu.meaning: نبی ایوب علیہ السلام سے مشتق، معنی صبر و استقامت
in_urdu.long_meaning: ایوب ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، اور نبی ایوب علیہ السلام سے مشتق ہے، جو قرآن کریم میں انبیاء سورة، آیت 83-84 میں ذکر کیا گیا ہے، یہ نام صبر و استقامت، اور دکھوں و مصائب سے صبر کرنے کی معنا رکھتا ہے، اسلامی تقالید میں اس نام کو بڑی اہمیت حاصل ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلم کمیونٹی میں.

in_hindi.name: एयुब
in_hindi.meaning: नबी एयुब से लिया गया, अर्थ धैर्य और दृढ़ता
in_hindi.long_meaning: एयुब एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है, और यह नबी एयुब से संबंधित है जिनका उल्लेख कुरआन में है, यह नाम धैर्य और दृढ़ता का प्रतीक है, भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में इस नाम का विशेष महत्व है, और यह नाम धार्मिक और आध्यात्मिक दृष्टिकोण से भी महत्वपूर्ण माना जाता है.

in_pashto.meaning: د نبي ایوب څخه اخستل شوی، معنی یې صبر او استقامت
in_pashto.long_meaning: ایوب یو مذکر نوم دی چی د عربي ژبې څخه اخستل شوی دی، او د نبي ایوب څخه مشتق شوی دی، چی د قران کریم په انبیاء سورت، آیت 83-84 کې ذکر شوی دی، دا نوم د صبر او استقامت، او د مشکلاتو څخه د صبر کولو معنی لري، په افغان او پښتون دود کې دا نوم ډیره اهمیت لري.

in_english.name: Eyub
in_english.meaning: Derived from Prophet Eyub, signifies patience and perseverance
in_english.long_meaning: Eyub is a masculine name originating from Arabic, derived from the name of Prophet Eyub (Job), mentioned in the Quran, Surah Anbiya, verses 83-84. The name signifies patience, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of adversity. It holds significant religious and spiritual importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing the values of endurance and faith. The name Eyub is used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting its universal appeal and timeless relevance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eyub holds significant cultural importance in the Muslim world. In numerous Islamic stories, Eyub is depicted as a symbol of patience, resilience, and perseverance. Hagar's journey to the desert, where she gave birth to Ishmael and Eyub, is considered as an example of faith and determination. Moreover, the central location of Mecca, the holiest city in Islam, in the Arabian Peninsula, reaffirms the important connection between Eyub's story and Islamic cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Eyub lies primarily in the story of Ibrahim and Hagar in the Quran. Their unwavering faith, despite adversity, is seen as a reminder for believers to trust in Allah's guidance and to have patience during difficult times. Furthermore, Eyub's name itself means 'living one', emphasizing the belief that life continues, sometimes in unexpected ways, even during the most challenging circumstances. This name carries a powerful message that, no matter the obstacles one may face, faith, patience, and determination will ultimately lead to a better life.

historical_references.reference: The tomb of Eyub is located in Istanbul, Turkey, and is considered one of the most important sites in Islam. It is said that Eyub was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and was killed during the Battle of Harrah in 657 AD. He was later buried at his current site below the Edirne city walls.
historical_references.context: Battle of Harrah, companion of the Prophet Muhammad

historical_references.reference: During the Ottoman Empire, the tomb of Eyub was a site of pilgrimage for both Sunni and Shia Muslims. It is said that the Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II, who conquered Constantinople in 1453, visited the tomb and was granted a vision of the Prophet Muhammad during his prayer there.
historical_references.context: Ottoman Empire, site of pilgrimage for Sunni and Shia Muslims

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Eyub, which is synonymous with the biblical figure Jacob's son Joseph who was sold into slavery in Egypt but later rose to become a powerful advisor, has a significant place in Islamic tradition. In modern context, the name Eyub is frequently mentioned in various Islamic platforms, including social media, websites, blogs, and print and electronic media. The modern usage of the name Eyub is primarily associated with its spiritual significance in Islamic tradition, specifically in the context of the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca known as the Hajj. The name Eyub is also used to commemorate the trials and sacrifices of the Prophet Ibrahim and his family. For instance, the location where the Prophet Ibrahim is believed to have thrown Hajar, his wife, into the well to quench her thirst is known as the Zamzam well, situated in the holy city of Mecca. The name Eyub is also used to refer to the area around this well. Thus, the name Eyub is an important part of Islamic heritage and continues to be relevant in contemporary discourse and cultural practices.
